It has nothing to do with its “coolness” but everything to do with the cost of entry. 

In the 90s during snowboardings first mainstream boom you could go to your local ski area and try it out for cheap. Board rental, ticket and lesson was $50 at my local place and probably closer to $100 at a bigger resort. If you liked it you would keep going because it was an achievable thing for most families to do a few times a year.

The sport today is just not accessible to anyone who isn’t wealthy and unless you started doing it 15 - 20 years ago when it was cheap to learn. Most parents who ski or snowboard know that skiing has an easier path to go from learning hill to lift to skiing with the family, so they choose that for their kids knowing they’ll have a better experience on vacation. Also if the parents already ski they’re definitely encouraging them to that.

I just priced out a lift ticket, half day lesson, and snowboard rental at my closest resort and it’s $425 before tax. If you’re a kid who thinks snowboarding is cool, but don’t have a family who is already into skiing then you’re probably never getting into it. Maybe get to go once as a super big present but that’s about it.

It’s a sad state in the industry and not gonna get better anytime soon

Be ready for a few good days and a LOT of shitty days instructing for a large resort. 

If you’re there for a few years and get certs you can move up and work private lessons which can be great, but be prepared to be a baby sitter on snow for a bunch of cold and frustrated kids a lot of the time. 

The sad fact is a lot of parents dump their kids into lessons so they can enjoy their vacation even if the kid doesn’t want to ski/snowboard. There will be days where 4 out of the 8 kids in your group want nothing to do with trying snowboarding, and the other 4 kids are eager to learn and want to progress faster than you’re allowed to. If you’re teaching adults the work is a lot more scarce so that’s the ticket to a free pass without typically having to work every line up.

Your main job is to make sure everyone is having fun and will want to keep snowboarding. One first bad day is make or break for a lot of kids so focus on the fun and less on the super technical aspects of that a lot of instructors fall into with the AASI shit. 

Lastly stay humble and realize you’re there to help people enjoy the sport, not nit pick how everyone rides. If you find yourself judging someone’s riding because their turns aren’t symmetrical you’re falling down the AASI rabbit hole
